Antecedentes Clínicos:
Rotura meniscal y lesión condral lateral de la rodilla derecha.
Hallazgos:
Ligamentos cruzados y colaterales sin alteraciones.
Menisco medial de morfología y señal conservada, sin signos de rotura.
Rotura compleja del cuerno anterior y cuerpo del menisco lateral con segmento que se insinúa al
receso menisco tibial a nivel del cuerpo. Leve extrusión meniscal difusa.
Úlceras condrales de espesor parcial y total de la zona de carga del compartimento femorotibial
lateral, de hasta aproximadamente 7 x 5 mm en sus ejes anteroposterior y mediolateral
respectivamente a nivel de la región posterior de carga del cóndilo femoral lateral, con cambios
óseos secundarios.
Cartílagos del compartimento femorotibial medial y patelofemoral sin alteraciones significativas.
Mínimo derrame articular. No hay quistes poplíteos.
Edema del paquete adiposo retro cuadricipital suprarrotuliano.
Tendones cuadricipital, rotuliano, tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial
dentro de límites normales.
Impresión:
Rotura compleja del menisco lateral con segmento que se insinúa al receso menisco tibial a nivel
del cuerpo. Leve extrusión meniscal difusa.
Condropatía lesiones grado 3 y 4 del compartimento femorotibial lateral.
Mínimo derrame articular.
Edema del paquete adiposo retro cuadricipital suprarrotuliano, hallazgos que podría representar
fenómenos de mal alineamiento rotuliano.

MRI of right Knee with 
-Locator, SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS, SG T1W


> Small size of lateral meniscus with absent bow-tie sign, in favor of lateral meniscus tear.
> Linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, without significant extending into the surface, in favor of  grade 2 intrasubstance signal of posterior horn of medial meniscus, maybe due to degeneration.
> Wearing of articular cartilage and subchondral bone marrow edeama, especially at lateral aspect of knee joint; large spur formation.
   Wearing articular cartilage of patella and spur, in favor of grade 3 patellar chondromalacia.
> The contour of ACL and PCL is in a straight line but increase signal intensity inside, in favor of grade 1 injury.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with thick suprapatellar, lateral and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.

Impression: 
1. Lateral meniscus tear.
2. Osteoarthritis of right knee joint, more severe at lateral compartment.
3. Synovitis of right knee and complex patellar plicae and suprapatellar burisitis.
4. Grade 3 patellar chondromalacia.
5. Grade 1 injury of ACL and PCL.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation and further management

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: [REDACTED]. Pain at the outer aspect. 
Comparison: [REDACTED].

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:
OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Alignment is anatomic. No acute fracture or bone bruise. Background marrow signal is normal without infiltrative marrow process. No aggressive osseous lesions.

JOINT SPACE:
Small joint effusion. No intra-articular bodies. Small, partially ruptured Baker's cyst with synovial proliferation.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: Chondral fraying at the anterior weightbearing medial femoral condyle. The tibial plateau cartilage is intact. No full-thickness defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: Diffuse partial-thickness patellar cartilage loss with small areas of full-thickness fissuring at the medial facet with associated subchondral cystic change/edema. The trochlear cartilage is intact.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. No patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 11 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
Nonspecific prepatellar subcutaneous edema about the knee. No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:

1.	Moderate patellofemoral and mild medial compartment chondrosis.
2.	Small joint effusion and small partially ruptured Baker's cyst.
3.	No acute fracture, meniscal tear or ligamentous injury.

CLINICAL HISTORY:One-year history of right knee pain with instability.

PROCEDURE:Multisequence, multiplanar unenhanced MRI of the right knee according to routine protocol.

IMAGING FINDINGS:

Nondiagnostic scout localizing images reviewed.

Complex tear posterior horn medial meniscus consistent with a focal radial tear as well as inferiorly surfacing oblique tear, the latter extending into the medial meniscal body which is slightly peripherally extruded. The posterior root is intact. The anterior horn is intact.

The lateral meniscus is intact.

Intact anterior cruciate ligament and posterior cruciate ligament.

Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the proximal tibial mid fibers of the superficial medial collateral ligament. Components of the deep medial collateral ligament including the posterior oblique ligament are intact.

The fibular collateral ligament is intact. Mild popliteus tendinosis without tear. Biceps femoris tendon insertion is intact. The iliotibial band is intact.

Minimal lateral patellar subluxation. The patellar retinacula are intact. No femoral trochlear dysplasia. The TT-TG distance measures 16 mm, above the upper limit of normal. The patellar retinacula are intact.

The quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact.

Mild patellofemoral chondrosis. Mild to moderate medial femorotibial chondrosis with subtle cartilage thinning. Mild lateral femorotibial chondrosis.

Trace knee joint fluid. Regional musculature is within normal limits. No suspicious focal marrow signal alteration. 

IMPRESSION:
1. Complex tear posterior horn medial meniscus with slight medial meniscal extrusion.
2. Mild to moderate tricompartment chondrosis most pronounced along the medial femorotibial compartment suggesting evolving mild osteoarthritis of the right knee.
3. Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the superficial medial collateral ligament. Component of the deep medial collateral ligament are intact.
4. Mild popliteus tendinosis without tear.
5. Lateralization of the tibial tubercle, which may predispose to patellofemoral maltracking/instability. At most minimal lateral patellar subluxation.

Technique: MRI of the knee. ACL normal. MCL normal. Medial meniscus normal. Lateral meniscus tear woth paramenisceal cyst. Incipient chondromalacia of lateral compartment. No baker's cyst. No effusion. Conclusion: Lateral meniscus tear woth paramenisceal cyst. Incipient chondromalacia of lateral compartment.
